title: Fixed-Node Quadrature for the Shape Likelihood

# Fixed-Node Quadrature for the Shape Likelihood

::: {.callout-note}
This page documents [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorFixedQuad]], a sibling of
[[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorQuad]] and the series-based schemes described in
[A Small-Shear Series Marginalization](wl_shape_marginalization_series.qmd):
same exact integral, no series truncation in $g$ anywhere, but FIXED node
counts instead of Quad's adaptive Divonne cubature. Unlike
[[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSeriesLensed]] (which caches a *truncated
polynomial* approximation to a function that must stay positive, and so is
guarded against — but not immune to — crossing zero at large $g$), this
class removes the polynomial altogether. See
`docs/theory/wl_shape_factor_history.md` for the design history behind this
class, including an earlier, geometry-branch-based version replaced by the
design described here.
:::

## Two fixed quadrature schemes, chosen per galaxy

$$
P(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} \mid g) = \int_{|\chi_I|<1} \mathrm{d}^2\chi_I\,
P_\mathrm{pop}(\chi_I)\, N_2\big(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - f_g(\chi_I);\,
\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2\big)
$$

is evaluated via one of two schemes, picked from
$(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs},\sigma_\mathrm{noise})$ alone — never $g$:

- **Two-panel $\psi$**, for a LOCALIZED noise kernel (most galaxies).
- **Native $\chi_I$-polar**, for a BROAD noise kernel — specifically when the
  entire unit disc lies within $N_\sigma\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ of
  $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$, i.e.
  $$1+|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}| \le N_\sigma\,\sigma_\mathrm{noise},
  \qquad N_\sigma=8.$$
  ($1+|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|$ is the distance from $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$
  to the farthest point of the unit disc — the diametrically opposite
  boundary point — so this condition says the noise kernel already covers
  the WHOLE disc, not just a neighborhood of $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$.)

Both are exact (no truncation, no linearization); the switch only picks
which fixed grid resolves a given galaxy's integrand well. Verified over an
840-case sweep (population shape, $|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|$,
$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$, $g$, both ellipticity conventions) that using
EITHER branch alone, unconditionally, produces a 15–17% worst case — always
in the OTHER branch's own regime — while the switch brings the combined
worst case down to 2.0%, median error around $10^{-6}$.

## Two-panel $\psi$

Same $\psi$-reparametrization [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorQuad]] uses:
$\chi_L=f_h(\psi)$, $h$ the shear with $f_h(0)=\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$
exactly, so $\psi=0$ always maps to the noise kernel's own peak. $\psi$ is
integrated in its own polar coordinates $(\rho,\theta)$, with $\rho$ split
into two independent Gauss–Legendre panels, $[0,R_\sigma)$ and
$[R_\sigma,1)$ (`n-radial` nodes each), concentrating resolution where the
noise kernel's mass actually is instead of spreading one rule uniformly
across the whole disc. $\theta$ is equally-spaced (`n-angular` nodes,
spectrally accurate for the smooth $2\pi$-periodic integrand) and offset by
$\phi=\arg\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ so a coarse grid stays exactly
rotation-covariant.

### $R_\sigma$: the exact split radius

$R_\sigma$ must contain the $\psi$-preimage of the physical noise disc
$\{\chi_L:|\chi_L-\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|\le N_\sigma\sigma_\mathrm{noise}\}$.
An earlier estimate used the map's local derivative at $\psi=0$ — cheap, but
badly overestimates the reach once $|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|$ gets close to
1, since it ignores the map's curvature entirely (verified: gives a
nonsensical value past the disc boundary, needing an ad hoc cap, for
$|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|=0.95$). Möbius maps send circles to circles
EXACTLY, so instead three points on the noise disc's own boundary are
mapped through $f_h^{-1}$ and circumscribed — recovering the true image
circle losslessly, no linearization or guessed direction involved:
$$
R_\sigma = \min\!\big(0.98,\ |c|+r\big),
$$
$c,r$ the center/radius of the circle through
$f_h^{-1}(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}+N_\sigma\sigma_\mathrm{noise}e^{i\theta_k})$
at $\theta_k=0,\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\tfrac{4\pi}{3}$. The $0.98$ cap only matters
when the noise disc already reaches the WHOLE unit disc from $\psi$'s own
side too — exactly the regime the native $\chi_I$ branch exists for instead
(see below).

### Puncture correction

Same mechanism as Quad: the integrand only ever evaluates the bracket
$N_2(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}-\chi_L)-N_0$, $N_0=N_2(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}-\chi_{L0})$,
$\chi_{L0}=f_g(0)$ (the population's own peak location under $g$, unrelated
to $h$), with $N_0$ added back once after the sum via
$\int P_\mathrm{pop}=1$ exactly. This makes the summed integrand finite
everywhere unconditionally — including for a [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapePopBeta]]
population with $\alpha<2$, whose area density $P_\mathrm{pop}(r)/(2\pi r)$
diverges at $r=0$, since EVERY domain node has some $g$ where the implied
$\chi_I(g,\chi_L)$ is exactly $0$.

## Native $\chi_I$-polar

When the noise kernel is broad enough to cover the whole disc, the
$\psi$-reparametrization's own Jacobian develops a huge (verified:
$\sim10^6\times$) dynamic range near the disc boundary, which no fixed
radial split resolves well. The fix is to not reparametrize at all: integrate
directly in $\chi_I$'s own polar coordinates instead, with FIXED nodes
$\chi_I=\rho\,e^{i\theta}$ ($\rho$: Gauss–Legendre on $[0,1)$; $\theta$:
equally-spaced, same $\phi$ offset as above).

Two simplifications follow, both because this grid is centered on
$\chi_I=0$ itself (unlike the two-panel grid, whose nodes are unrelated to
the population's own peak):

- **No Jacobian for the population term.** The quadrature measure's own
  $\rho\,\mathrm{d}\rho$ cancels $P_\mathrm{pop}(\rho)/(2\pi\rho)$'s
  $1/\rho$ analytically — the per-node weight is just
  $w_\rho w_\theta/(2\pi)$ times $P_\mathrm{pop}(\rho)$ directly, no
  $2\pi\rho$ division anywhere.
- **No puncture correction.** The noise kernel
  $N_2(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}-f_g(\chi_I))$ is evaluated PLAINLY (never
  subtracted from a baseline) — a bounded exponential, safe on its own,
  since there is no unrelated singular point anywhere in this domain to
  protect against (unlike two-panel's $\chi_{L0}$). This was the surprising
  finding: dropping the correction entirely still converges cleanly even on
  the Beta $\alpha=1.55$ case that originally motivated it (0.025% at
  $n=15\!\times\!15$ down to 0.00008% at $n=100\!\times\!100$) — in
  hindsight, that correction was only ever needed because an earlier design
  gridded in $\chi_L$-space and inverted to $\chi_I$, which unevenly
  sparsified nodes near the singularity; gridding natively in $\chi_I$ from
  the start never has that problem.

## `use-marginal-spline`: caching the marginal as a function of $g$

Both branches share the same per-galaxy domain cache (`n-radial`/`n-angular`
sized nodes, rebuilt only when $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$/$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$
change, never $g$) and the same opt-in `use-marginal-spline` mechanism:
$\ln P(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}\mid g)$ cached as a bivariate function of $g$
over $[-g_\mathrm{max},g_\mathrm{max}]^2$ (`spline-g-max`), built lazily via
this codebase's autoknots 2D spline machinery for populations whose area
density stays bounded at $r=0$, or a plain fixed-knot grid (never adaptive,
cannot abort) for populations that diverge there — see the class' own C
docs for why that divergence check only ever matters for the two-panel
branch, and is (conservatively, not incorrectly) applied regardless of
which branch a given galaxy actually uses.

## Verified regimes

All checked against both an independent scipy disc integral and the real
`Quad` C class:

- Real and complex $g$ through $|g|=0.99$ (well past where the series
  schemes' truncated polynomial crosses zero) — accurate to
  $\sim10^{-9}$, no crash.
- $|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|$ from near-zero to $0.99$, at every tested
  $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ (both regimes, and the switch boundary between
  them) — no discontinuity in the likelihood across the branch switch
  (checked directly: the change in $-2\ln P$ across a $10^{-4}$ step
  straddling the boundary is an ordinary, small amount, not a jump).
- Both ellipticity conventions ([[numcosmo|NcGalaxyWLObsEllipConv]]
  `TRACE` and `TRACE_DET`).
- Any population (not just Gaussian): each node evaluates
  `nc_galaxy_shape_pop_eval_p()` directly, the same convention `Quad`
  uses — unlike `SeriesLensed`, there is no Taylor-composition step
  requiring an analytic population form, so no Gaussian-only guard.

## {#sec-limits} Limitation: narrow populations

A fixed grid cannot resolve a population much narrower than its node
spacing, shared by both branches — the same blind spot an earlier,
fixed-degree version of `Quad` itself had, which is exactly why `Quad`
moved to adaptive Divonne cubature with explicit peak hints. Production
only ever uses a Gaussian population with
$\sigma_\mathrm{pop}\in(0.2,0.4)$ — comfortably inside the validated
regime; use `Quad` for narrower or more exotic populations.

## `n-radial`/`n-angular`

Both properties are `CONSTRUCT_ONLY` and size whichever grid is actually
chosen: `n-radial` nodes PER PANEL for two-panel (so $2\times$`n-radial`
radial nodes total), or `n-radial` nodes in the one grid for native $\chi_I$.
Default 15 for both, validated across the regimes above.

See `tests/python/nc/lss/galaxy/test_galaxy_shape_factor_fixed_quad.py` for
the full test suite this page's numbers are drawn from, including
`nc_galaxy_shape_factor_fixed_quad_eval_two_panel()`/`_eval_chi_i_native()`,
test-only accessors that force one branch regardless of the switch, used
there to characterize each branch's own accuracy outside its intended
regime directly.
